territorial_scope.description: Applies to impersonation conduct in or affecting U.S. commerce as defined in the Federal Trade Commission Act.

evidence.quote: in or affecting commerce as commerce is defined in the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 44)

summary.short: Final FTC trade regulation rule, effective April 1, 2024, that makes it an unfair or deceptive act or practice to materially and falsely pose as, or misrepresent affiliation with, a government or business or its officers in or affecting commerce. Proposed §461.4 (means and instrumentalities) is not finalized.
summary.long: Final rule of the Federal Trade Commission (16 CFR Part 461), issued under section 18 of the FTC Act and effective April 1, 2024. Section 461.1 defines 'business' (including not-for-profit entities), 'government', 'materially' and 'officer'. Section 461.2 makes it an unfair or deceptive act or practice to materially and falsely pose as, or materially misrepresent affiliation or endorsement with, a government entity or officer, in or affecting commerce. Section 461.3 applies the same prohibition to businesses. The final text replaces 'unlawful' with 'unfair or deceptive act or practice' and adds 'materially' and 'in or affecting commerce' to track section 5 of the FTC Act. The proposed means-and-instrumentalities provision (proposed § 461.4) is not finalized and is addressed in a separate supplemental proposal. The rule contains no reporting or recordkeeping requirements. The preamble says the rule lets the Commission seek monetary relief and civil penalties more efficiently; the regulatory text sets no penalty amounts.

notes: Annotated from the Federal Register final rule text (89 FR 15017, 1 March 2024). The operative provisions are 16 CFR 461.1 to 461.3; proposed 461.4 (means and instrumentalities) was not finalized, and the preamble, Chair statement and footnotes are context only. The Chair statement is not part of the CFR. Section 461.1 defines business to include not-for-profit entities. The preamble states the rule imposes no disclosure or recordkeeping requirements. The Summary's general wording on prohibiting impersonation applies only to sections 461.2 and 461.3, since 461.4 was not finalized.

evidence.quote: Friday, March 1, 2024
This rule is effective April 1, 2024.
Business means a corporation, partnership, association, or any other entity that provides goods or services, including not-for-profit entities.
Government includes federal, state, local, and tribal governments as well as agencies and departments thereof.
Materially means likely to affect a person’s choice of, or conduct regarding, goods or services.
Officer includes executives, officials, employees, and agents.
as commerce is defined in the Federal Trade Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 44)

obligations.summary: Prohibits any person in or affecting commerce from materially and falsely posing as a government entity or officer, or materially misrepresenting affiliation with, endorsement or sponsorship by a government entity or officer (§ 461.2(a)-(b)); the rule applies to any actor in commerce, not only firms.

evidence.quote: materially and falsely pose as, directly or by implication, a government entity or officer thereof

obligations.summary: Prohibits any person in or affecting commerce from materially and falsely posing as a business or officer thereof, or materially misrepresenting affiliation with, endorsement or sponsorship by a business or officer thereof (§ 461.3(a)-(b)); 'business' includes not-for-profit entities (§ 461.1).

evidence.quote: materially and falsely pose as, directly or by implication, a business or officer thereof

enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of 16 CFR 461.2 or 461.3 (material false impersonation or misrepresentation of affiliation with a government or business), where the violator has actual knowledge or knowledge fairly implied that the act is unfair or deceptive and prohibited by the rule

thresholds.note: The rule states no numeric cutoff at which legal treatment changes. Dollar figures and counts in the preamble describe consumer losses, comments and economic analysis, not legal treatment. Civil penalty amounts are not stated in the regulatory text.
